• Also, to indicate **time reference** ''**for**'' and ''**since**'' are used in the past perfect continuous tense and it describes **when the action started and how long it continued in the past**.
 
• The past perfect continuous tense is constructed using **had + been + the verb’s present participle **(here, **playing**).

 

Hence, the correct answer is option 2.

Correct sentence: *He said **he had been** playing tennis since he was eight*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/51867102c7c2f369f6e29d2efe025e3b3367c68261ec20262828d84ca5c8f854.png] **Hinglish__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the underlined segment, the use of the gerund 'buying' and the **determiner 'few'** is incorrect.
 
• A **gerund** is a **verb form that functions as a noun **and is** not required **as per the context of the sentence.
 
• The **to-infinitive** should be used **in place of** the **gerund 'buying'**.
 
• The to-infinitive is used in many sentence constructions, often expressing the purpose of something or someone's opinion about something.
 
• The to-infinitive is formed as to + base form of the verb (here, buy).
 
• Also, in the given sentence, the **noun 'milk' **is an **uncountable noun**.
 
• The **determiner ''few''** is applied to countable objects while the **determiner ''some''** is applicable to **both countable and uncountable objects**.

Hence, the correct answer is option 4.

Correct Sentence: *I went to the market **to buy some** vegetables and milk*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/51867102c7c2f369f6e29d2efe025e3b3367c68261ec20262828d84ca5c8f854.png] **Hinglish__**

 
• रेखांकित खंड में, gerund 'buying' और determiner 'few' का उपयोग गलत है।
 
• Gerund एक क्रिया रूप है जो संज्ञा के रूप में कार्य करता है और वाक्य के संदर्भ के अनुसार इसकी आवश्यकता नहीं है।
 
• Gerund 'buying' के स्थान पर to-infinitive का उपयोग किया जाना चाहिए।
 
• To-infinitive का उपयोग कई वाक्य निर्माणों में किया जाता है, जो अक्सर **किसी चीज़ के उद्देश्य या किसी चीज़ के बारे में किसी की राय व्यक्त करते हैं**।
 
• To-infinitive: to + base form of the verb (यहाँ, buy) के रूप में बनता है।
 
• साथ ही दिए गए वाक्य में **'milk' संज्ञा** एक uncountable** संज्ञा **है।
 
• Determiner ''few'' countable objects पर लागू होता है जबकि determiner ''some'' countable और uncountable वस्तुओं दोनों पर लागू होता है।

 

अत: सही उत्तर विकल्प 4 है।

सही वाक्य: *I went to the market to buy some vegetables and milk*.

By BODMAS rule

11 + 4 – 3 × 0.43 = 8

11 + 4 – 1.29 = 8

15 – 1.29 = 8

13.71 = 8 (LHS ≠ RHS)

**Option 2 : **+ and ÷

Given:

2.75 – 3 + 3 × 7 = 8

**Given:**

**11 + 4 - 3 ÷ 3 × 7 = 8**

**11 + 4 × 3 ÷ 3 - 7 = 8**

**By BODMAS rule**

**11 + 4 × 1 - 7 = 8**

**11 + 4 – 7 = 8**

**15 – 7 = 8**

**8 = 8 (LHS = RHS)**

**Option 4 :** + and ×

Given:

11 + 4 - 3 ÷ 3 × 7 = 8

After interchange the signs;

11 × 4 - 3 ÷ 3 + 7 = 8

By BODMAS rule

11 × 4 - 1 + 7 = 8

44 - 1 + 7 = 8

51 – 1 = 8

50 = 8 (LHS ≠ RHS)

Hence, the answer is **“****- and ×****”**.

questions.question: The incomes of A and B are in the ratio 6 ∶ 11. The ratio of their expenditures is 1 ∶ 2. If A and B save Rs. 9,000 and Rs. 11,500, respectively, then the expenditure of B is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Apply **Cross-Multiplication** method on Income and Expenditure ratios:

Ratio difference: (6 × 2) − (11 × 1) = 1 unit

Value difference: |(1 × 11,500) − (2 × 9,000)| = |11,500 − 18,000| = 6,500

1 unit = 6,500 ⇒ Income of A = 6 × 6,500 = 39,000

Expenditure of B = 2 × (Income of A − Savings of A) = 2 × (39,000 − 9,000) = 2 × 30,000

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 60000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of **Income** (A : B) = 6 : 11

Ratio of **Expenditure** (A : B) = 1 : 2

**Savings** of A = Rs. 9,000 | **Savings** of B = Rs. 11,500

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a140ee5c355e3f2068ecf538a37c57de5ab6df34e2727d929e876a0cee4e693b.png] 

**Formula:** **Income** − **Expenditure** = **Savings**

⇒ Let **Income** of A and B be 6x and 11x respectively.

⇒ Let **Expenditure** of A and B be y and 2y respectively.

⇒ Equation 1 (A): 6x − y = 9,000

⇒ Equation 2 (B): 11x − 2y = 11,500

⇒ Multiplying Equation 1 by 2: 12x − 2y = 18,000

⇒ Subtracting Equation 2 from Equation 1: (12x − 2y) − (11x − 2y) = 18,000 − 11,500

⇒ x = 6,500

⇒ Substituting x in Eq 1: 6(6,500) − y = 9,000

⇒ 39,000 − y = 9,000

⇒ y = 30,000

⇒ **Expenditure** of B = 2y = 2 × 30,000 = 60,000

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 60000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Income, Expenditure, and Savings Relation

The fundamental relation is **Income = Expenditure + Savings**. If any two components or their ratios are given, the third can be determined.

Ratio of Components

When income and expenditure ratios are given for two people with specific savings, the **Cross-Product Method** is the fastest way to find the absolute values of income.

Savings % = (**Savings** ÷ **Income**) × 100. This is often used in data interpretation and percentage-based income questions.</p
